title: The judge token can be guessed without limit on POST /runs and cancel
body:
## Summary
POST /runs and POST /runs/<id>/cancel compare a bearer token in constant time but count nothing, so a stranger can try tokens as fast as the socket allows.

## Description
src/athena/proving/server/app.py:172-182 `_token_ok` compares with secrets.compare_digest and returns; src/athena/proving/server/app.py:267-277 `_authorized` answers 401 and keeps no state. The token is chosen by the operator (PROVING_JUDGE_TOKEN, any length), and a correct guess starts runs that spend the day's Nemotron cap. The obvious fix (a failure counter with a lockout) lets the same stranger lock the real judge out, so the shape is a policy call: per-client backoff (needs the client address, see the audit card), a global slow-down after N failures, or a minimum token length enforced at start. Technique: none in this context's subjects; rate-limiting is the nearest subject in the registry.

## Flow
- stranger loops POST /runs with Authorization: Bearer <guess>
- app._authorized -> _token_ok -> 401, nothing recorded, no delay
- a hit starts a run; repeated hits spend the day's cap ($3 Nemotron by default)
- fix options in build order: refuse a token under N chars at start; a global failure budget per minute answering 429; per-client backoff if the address is recorded

## Expected impact
The operator of a hosted page; measured as guesses per second the server answers (unbounded today). Could break: a judge who mistypes the token a few times meets a 429, and a lockout design could let strangers deny the real judge.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the trigger cannot be brute-forced at socket speed
Before: probe by reading: 0 of 2 bearer doors count failures (app.py:172, :267)
After: predicted: failures past a budget answer 429 with Retry-After; a short token refused at start
Method: simulation - which shape is right (lockout, global budget, per-client) is a policy decision with a denial-of-service trade-off, so no figure was taken
Result: better
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence: src/athena/proving/server/app.py:172-182 `return secrets.compare_digest(...) and bool(expected)` (no counter); src/athena/proving/server/app.py:267-277 `_authorized` 401 path keeps no state; README §9 / ADR 0037: the page is public

title: No record says who started or cancelled a run, or that a token was refused
body:
## Summary
The trigger page logs nothing: request logging is silenced, so a started or cancelled run and every refused token attempt leave no trace beyond the run directory itself.

## Description
src/athena/proving/server/app.py:115-117 `log_message` returns without writing (to keep the Authorization header out of logs), and no other line in app.py or runner.py prints on a POST. A run that spent money has its own directory, but a cancel, a 401/403 storm, a 429 at the cap or a 502 start failure exists nowhere after the response. Fixed looks like one stderr line per POST outcome (route, status, error code, run id) with no header and no body. Whether it also carries the client address is the decision: it is what makes a guessing storm attributable, and it is a stranger's data kept by the operator.

## Flow
- a judge cancels a run; a stranger sends 10,000 wrong tokens
- app.do_POST answers 200 / 401; log_message is a no-op
- afterwards nothing on the host says either happened
- fix: one structured line per POST outcome to stderr, no Authorization, no body

## Expected impact
The operator reading a hosted container's logs after an odd day; measured as POST outcomes that leave a line (0 of 11 outcome statuses today). Could break: nothing functional; a log that includes addresses keeps strangers' data.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a privileged act and a refused one each leave a line
Before: 0 of 11 POST outcome statuses (202, 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 429, 502, 503) write anything (read app.py:115, :293-343)
After: predicted 11 of 11 with route, status and error code
Method: simulation - the line is S to build, but what it may record about a stranger (address or not) is the operator's privacy call
Result: better
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence: src/athena/proving/server/app.py:115-117 `def log_message(...): return`; git grep -n 'print(' src/athena/proving/server/app.py src/athena/proving/server/runner.py -> no hit

title: Cancel and stop kill the run's process but not the claude children it spawned
body:
## Summary
Runner.cancel and Runner.stop kill the `python -m athena.proving` child only; on a full (non-hosted) host its `claude -p` grandchildren keep running to their own timeout after the run is reported cancelled.

## Description
src/athena/proving/server/runner.py popen starts the child with no process group (no start_new_session / CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP), and cancel/stop call process.kill() (runner.py:568-582), which is SIGKILL or TerminateProcess on that one pid. The child runs the Haiku control and judges through src/athena/proving/roles.py subprocess_runner (subprocess.run with a timeout the parent enforces) and Athena-on-Claude through SubprocessTransport; once the parent is killed nothing enforces those timeouts or reaps them. Technique: subprocess-lifecycle / termination-and-reaping (kill the tree, not the leader).

## Flow
- a full-mode Gauntlet is running the control on four workers
- a judge presses Cancel -> runner.cancel -> process.kill()
- the run is reported cancelled; up to four claude -p children keep running and billing the subscription until their own timeouts
- fix in build order: start the child in its own process group/session; cancel and stop kill the group; a test with a fake run that spawns a sleeping grandchild

## Expected impact
The operator on a full host (the hosted container runs no claude); measured as grandchildren alive after cancel. Could break: a group kill on Windows needs CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP plus taskkill /T or a job object, which is the M part.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a cancelled run leaves no process behind
Before: by reading: 0 of 2 kill paths (cancel, stop) reach grandchildren; up to --workers (4) claude children per run
After: predicted 0 grandchildren alive after cancel
Method: simulation - the instrument (a fake run spawning a grandchild, checked after cancel, on both Windows and POSIX) was not built in this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/athena/proving/server/runner.py:303-316 popen (no start_new_session, no creationflags); runner.py:568-571 stop -> job.process.kill(); runner.py:581-582 cancel -> job.process.kill(); src/athena/proving/roles.py:276-288 subprocess.run(..., timeout=timeout)
instrument: tests/proving/test_server.py: a FAKE_RUN variant that spawns a grandchild sleeping 5 s then writing a file; cancel; assert the file never appears (red today)

title: A run whose report fails to load keeps the previous run's headline on the page
body:
## Summary
When a picked run's report cannot be read, the page clears the drill-down but leaves the previous run's headline and notes in place, so two runs read as one.

## Description
src/athena/proving/server/static/index.html:822-836 select(): state.selected and the row highlight move to the new run, renderHeadline/renderNotes run only on success, and the catch writes 'This run has no readable report' into #drill alone. #headline (the big verdict number) and #notes still show the last run that loaded, under the new run's highlighted row. Fixed looks like the catch also rendering the headline and notes for 'no readable report' (renderHeadline(null)-like state naming the run).

## Flow
- open run A (loads), then click run B whose report.json is unreadable or incomplete (404 no_report)
- select(B) -> getJSON throws -> only #drill changes
- the page shows A's verdict beside B's highlighted row

## Expected impact
A judge reading the hosted page; measured as surfaces left stale on a failed load (2 of 3 today). Could break: nothing.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a failed load never shows another run's verdict
Before: by reading: 2 of 3 surfaces (headline, notes) keep the previous run on failure
After: predicted 0 of 3
Method: simulation - the page has no DOM harness (no jsdom/happy-dom test for this file); the S instrument is that harness
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/athena/proving/server/static/index.html:822-836 (catch only clears #drill); :830-832 renderHeadline/renderNotes inside the try
instrument: a DOM test of index.html's script (happy-dom or jsdom under the workspace vitest) with fetch stubbed: load run A, then fail run B, assert #headline no longer shows A

title: History rows open only on Enter and announce no action
body:
## Summary
The run history's rows are focusable `tr` elements that open a run on click or Enter, but not Space, and expose no button role, so keyboard and screen-reader users meet a row with no stated action.

## Description
src/athena/proving/server/static/index.html:691-692 builds each row with tabindex 0, onclick and an onkeydown that handles only Enter. A screen reader announces a table row; nothing says it opens the run, and Space (the key users press on a focused control) scrolls the page instead. Fixed looks like a real <button> in the Run cell carrying the action (the row stays a row) or role/aria-label plus Space handling.

## Flow
- Tab to a history row; press Space -> the page scrolls
- a screen reader says 'row' with the date and id, no action
- fix: a button in the first cell opens the run; the row's click stays as a pointer shortcut

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader judges; measured as rows whose action is announced (0 of N). Could break: row styling if the button is not reset.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - each history row exposes an announced, keyboard-complete action
Before: by reading: 0 of N rows announce an action; Space unhandled
After: predicted N of N
Method: simulation - no DOM or axe harness exists for this page in the round
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: the same DOM harness as the stale-headline card, plus axe-core over the rendered history table

title: The verdict strip's attack buttons are 12px targets 3px apart
body:
## Summary
Each attack in the headline strip is a 12x12px button with a 3px gap, under WCAG 2.5.8's 24px minimum target size, on the page's main visual.

## Description
src/athena/proving/server/static/index.html:129 `.cell { width: 12px; height: 12px; }` and :128 `.cells { gap: 3px }`; each cell is a button that opens its attack (index.html:413-416). On a phone a judge taps a neighbour as often as the cell. The spacing exception does not apply (a 24px circle on each target overlaps its neighbours). The density is the strip's design (one square per driven attack, a run drives up to hundreds), so the fix is a design call: larger cells under the 520px breakpoint, or keep the strip as a picture and move the action to the list below.

## Flow
- open the hosted page on a phone; tap one square in the strip
- the 12px target and 3px gap make the neighbour as likely a hit

## Expected impact
Judges on phones; measured as targets under 24px (every cell today). Could break: the strip's one-glance density.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - each tappable square meets the minimum target size
Before: every cell is 12x12 with a 3px gap (index.html:128-129)
After: not taken
Method: simulation - the choice (bigger cells vs a non-interactive strip) is a design call and is seen only in a browser
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence: src/athena/proving/server/static/index.html:128 `.cells { ... gap: 3px; ...}`; :129 `.cell { width: 12px; height: 12px; ...}`; :413-416 verdictCell builds a button

title: The Sandboxes spike uploads gitignored files beside the source it packs
body:
## Summary
`python -m athena.proving.sandbox spike` tars every file under the directories it names, gitignored ones included, and uploads the tarball to a third-party service.

## Description
src/athena/proving/sandbox/__main__.py:43-56 pack() walks DAEMON_PATHS and APP_PATHS and skips only node_modules, .next and caches (_SKIP). Today that sends examples/ledgerbox/data/ledgerbox.sqlite (gitignored, `git status --ignored`) to Token Factory Sandboxes, and a future examples/ledgerbox/.env.local would go the same way. Fixed looks like packing only what `git ls-files` lists under those paths (the repository as committed), with the skip list kept for a tree without git.

## Flow
- an operator runs the spike with --app
- pack(root, DAEMON_PATHS + APP_PATHS) adds examples/ledgerbox/data/*
- client.upload sends the tarball to the remote service

## Expected impact
The operator; measured as untracked files in the tarball (1 today: the app's local sqlite). Could break: a spike run from an export without .git, which the fallback covers.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the tarball holds exactly the committed tree
Before: by reading plus `git status --ignored examples/ledgerbox`: 1 ignored file packed
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - the S test needs a temporary git repository fixture; not built in this round
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: src/athena/proving/sandbox/__main__.py:40 `_SKIP = {"node_modules", ".next", ...}`; :54 archive.add(source, ..., filter=keep); `git status --porcelain --ignored examples/ledgerbox` -> `!! examples/ledgerbox/data/`
instrument: tests/proving/sandbox/test_sandbox_spike.py: a tmp git repo with one tracked and one ignored file under a packed path; assert only the tracked one is in pack()'s archive (red today)
